findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site where the 'embed_category' site setting has never been set. `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]` returns nil when no such site_settings row exists (the default install — embed_category was an optional setting with default ''), so `[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError on nil and `rake db:migrate` fails for every fresh/existing install that never configured embedding, blocking the entire deploy.

[BUG] The migration interpolates each migrated host value directly into a SQL string literal. A previously-saved embeddable_hosts entry containing a single quote (the old setting was free-text, e.g. `o'brien.example.com`) terminates the string literal and makes the INSERT raise a PostgreSQL syntax error, aborting db:migrate; it is also a raw SQL injection vector in the migration.

[BUG] update and destroy call methods on nil when no EmbeddableHost exists for params[:id]. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or invalid id makes `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` return nil, then `save_host(host)` does `host.host = ...` and `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of the 404 the admin API contract implies.

[ADVISORY] The `update` action performs no persistence — it re-serializes the freshly-fetched OpenStruct without applying params. The frontend's `saveChanges` (admin-embedding.js.es6 calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`) sends a PUT /admin/customize/embedding that silently does nothing; an admin who edits embedding-level settings and hits save gets a success response while no data is written — bitten the first time any embedding-level (non-host) setting is added to the UI backing this model.

[ADVISORY] The migration uses `create_table ... force: true` and embeds data-migration SQL inside a non-reversible `change` block. `force: true` drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table without warning (destroying data if one exists), and the destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings` plus INSERTs make `rake db:rollback` fail with IrreversibleMigration, leaving no downgrade path for an operator who needs to revert this feature.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes all four category fabricators from category_fabricator.rb and re-creates them in a new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, inverting which file owns which fabricator. The next developer looking for (or re-adding) category fabricators edits spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and finds only the embeddable_host fabricator; the cross-file swap also means this PR silently depends on embeddable_host_fabricator.rb being loaded for every suite that fabricates :category — a load-order/file-move away from undefined-fabricator failures across dozens of unrelated specs.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site setting has never been set (fresh installs and most existing installs). `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]` returns nil when no row exists, so `[0]['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError on nil and the entire migration (and the deploy) fails for any site that never configured embed_category — which is the default, since the setting's default was ''.

[BUG] update and destroy raise NoMethodError (500) when params[:id] does not match a record. `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a stale/already-deleted host, then `save_host(nil)` executes `host.host = ...` and `host.destroy` on nil, returning a 500 instead of a 404 the admin API contract implies; concurrent admin edits of the same host (both pressing delete) trigger this deterministically.

[BUG] Host values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated unescaped into raw SQL INSERTs. Any migrated host value containing a single quote (the old host_list setting allowed arbitrary lines) breaks the INSERT with a PG syntax error and aborts the migration mid-way, leaving the table created but the settings-delete at line 28 unexecuted; the site then has empty embeddable_hosts and all embeds start returning InvalidAccess.

[ADVISORY] The update action is a no-op that ignores its params, and the admin-embedding controller's saveChanges calls it with an empty payload — a ships-inert endpoint. PUT /admin/customize/embedding re-renders the current state without persisting anything, and no test in the diff asserts update behavior; an admin clicking any future 'save' on this screen silently saves nothing. If embedding-level settings are genuinely gone, both the action, the route, and the frontend saveChanges should be deleted; if they're coming, this is dead surface shipped now.

[ADVISORY] _focusOnInput is registered with both @on('didInsertElement') and @observes('editing'), so it fires on insert even when not editing (no .host-name input exists), and Ember.$('.host-name').focus() is a silent no-op selector miss. Every non-editing host row schedules an afterRender focus on an empty jQuery set; harmless today but the combined decorator usage means the focus also re-fires when editing toggles on rows other than the edited one in some Ember versions, and no test covers the focus behavior at all.

[ADVISORY] No uniqueness validation on host, and the format regex rejects some legitimate forms while allowing no internationalized hostnames. An admin can save the same host twice with different categories; record_for_host then returns an arbitrary one of them (.first with no order), so embedded topics land in a nondeterministic category. No spec in the diff covers duplicate hosts or the category-selection tiebreak.

[ADVISORY] The plural hydration branch deletes the *_ids key unconditionally and maps lookup misses to null entries instead of dropping them, unlike the singular branch which only deletes on successful hydration. A payload where a referenced id has no corresponding side-loaded record yields `colors: [null]` in the hydrated object, and downstream template iteration over the array renders nulls/crashes; the singular branch guards this case, the new plural branch does not — behavior divergence visible the first time a serializer emits an id without the matching sideload record.

[ADVISORY] The only coverage for the new CRUD controller is a subclass-inheritance assertion; create/update/destroy behavior (validation errors, category_id defaulting to uncategorized, serialization shape) is untested. The nil-id 500 in update/destroy and the blank-category fallback in save_host have no test to catch regressions; a future refactor of save_host ships red to admins unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The 'raises an error with a missing host' test no longer tests a distinct condition — with no EmbeddableHost rows the request fails for the same reason as the no-referer case, so the specific 'no hosts configured' acceptance criterion (previously the embeddable_hosts.blank? branch) has been dropped without replacement coverage. The behavioral guarantee 'embeds are refused when no host is configured' is now only incidentally covered; if host_allowed? were changed to return true for an empty set (e.g. an 'allow all' default reintroduced), no spec would fail.

[BUG] Admin::EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT and re-serializes the embedding without persisting any submitted attributes, so the update endpoint is a silent no-op. The frontend controller's saveChanges action calls embedding.update({}) which issues this PUT; any future settings save is silently discarded while the UI believes it saved — the endpoint enforces no invariant at all.

[ADVISORY] The saveChanges action has no corresponding button or invocation in embedding.hbs, making it dead code. The next developer adding an embedding-level setting will wire a button to a save action that round-trips to a no-op server endpoint (see EmbeddingController#update), shipping a broken save path; either delete it or implement the server side.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the embed_category site setting does not exist, because execute(...)[0]['id'] dereferences a missing row. Any install (including fresh ones, where embed_category was never set) fails the migration and blocks the entire deploy at db:migrate; the data-migration concern is bolted onto the schema change without guarding absence.

[BUG] update and destroy call .first on a where lookup and then act on the result without a nil check, raising NoMethodError for a nonexistent or stale id. A DELETE/PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with an id deleted in another tab returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404, and destroy additionally re-renders nothing after the exception.

[ADVISORY] Migrated host values are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT, so any quote character in the old embeddable_hosts setting value breaks the SQL. An admin whose legacy setting contained a stray quote (the old setting was freeform text) hits a SQL error mid-migration, leaving embeddable_hosts rows partially inserted before the settings rows are deleted.

[ADVISORY] The _hydrateEmbedded change to support plural _ids keys rewrites shared store hydration infrastructure, and the new plural branch unconditionally deletes the key even when _lookupSubType returns nothing, unlike the singular branch's guarded delete. Every model in the app with a *_ids attribute (not just embedding) now has that attribute silently stripped and replaced with a possibly-empty pluralized array; any payload using e.g. uploaded_ids now loses the raw value on the client. The behavioral drift between the two branches means the singular case preserves data on failed lookup while the plural case does not.

[ADVISORY] All category fabricators (diff_category, happy_category, private_category) were moved out of category_fabricator.rb and into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, inverting the dependency between the two fabricator files. Every developer adding a category fabricator will add it to the (now-empty-in-spirit) category_fabricator.rb or accidentally duplicate definitions across two files; the category definitions live in a file named for an unrelated model and must be kept in sync with the file they replaced.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? dropped the embeddable-hosts-present guard while the rest of the diff moved host configuration to the table, so the guard against misconfiguration now relies solely on has_topic_embed?. On a site where hosts were never configured but a stale TopicEmbed row exists (e.g. hosts deleted after embedding was used), expandable_first_post? now returns true and renders the expand/truncate UI for a topic whose referer check would deny embeds — a behavior change on a path not required by the category-per-host feature.

[BUG] The embeddable-host adapter's pathFor() returns the constant '/admin/customize/embedding' for every operation (create, update, destroy included), ignoring type and id. host.save() and destroyRecord() PUT/DELETE /admin/customize/embedding, which only has GET show and the no-op PUT update routes — a save resolves against the embedding update endpoint (which persists nothing) so edits silently never reach EmbeddableHostsController and the admin believes the host was saved; destroy 404s. The resources :embeddable_hosts routes are unreachable from this client.

[BUG] The migration backfills rows with raw SQL INSERTs carrying the raw site_setting value, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization (scheme/path stripping), while record_for_host matches with lower(host) = uri.host. A legacy setting value like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (exactly the forms the old setting and the diff's own specs show were in use) is stored verbatim, so after upgrade EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(referer) finds no row and every previously-working embed throws Discourse::InvalidAccess — a silent security-behavior regression for existing installs.

[BUG] has_many :embeddable_hosts uses embed: :ids, so the JSON payload carries only embeddable_host_ids with no side-loaded embeddable_hosts array, leaving the client nothing to hydrate the ids from. The store's _hydrateEmbedded plural branch maps each id through _lookupSubType against a root that contains no embeddable_host records, producing an embeddable_hosts array of undefined entries; the embedding admin page renders a row per undefined and crashes accessing host.host / host.isNew — the whole screen is broken.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no index on host (and none on category_id), while every embed/comments request queries where("lower(host) = ?"). Each embed request is an unindexed, non-sargable (lower(host)) full scan; duplicates of the same host are freely insertable since there is no unique constraint, so admins create conflicting category mappings that resolve to whichever row .first returns. Operators get nondeterministic category assignment on duplicate rows.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint and its client saveChanges() action are no-ops: update accepts no parameters, mutates nothing, and re-serializes the OpenStruct. The admin UI's save button (saveChanges in admin-embedding.js.es6) appears to succeed while persisting nothing, and the advertised update route is dead weight — a future maintainer adding a field to EmbeddingSerializer will find updates silently discarded because no assignment code exists anywhere.

[ADVISORY] update and destroy fetch with .first and dereference the result without a nil check. A stale admin tab or raced delete sends an id that no longer exists and gets a NoMethodError 500 (nil.host= / nil.destroy) instead of a 404; there is no find_record-style guard so the error contract for this endpoint is an unhandled exception.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the 'any embeddable host configured' guard, so it now returns true for any topic with a topic_embed whenever embed_truncate is on, with no live host requirement. Sites that truncate embeds but have since deleted all allowed hosts still serve truncated/expandable first posts for historical embedded topics; the check's semantics changed from 'embedding actively configured' to 'embedding was ever used', and no caller was updated for that narrowing of the guard.

[BUG] The migration permanently deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no down-migration and no archival, so the original configuration is irrecoverably destroyed the moment the migration runs. If the migration's data-copy logic misfires (e.g. the SQL-injection-prone string interpolation at line 28 hits a host value containing a quote and aborts mid-copy), the settings are already deleted and the operator's embed host list is lost; there is no rollback path since `change` provides only table-drop on rollback, not settings restoration.

[BUG] Host values read from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into a raw SQL INSERT string ("... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."), so any value containing a single quote or backslash breaks the insert. A site whose embeddable_hosts setting contains an entry with an apostrophe raises a PG error mid-migration, leaving the table half-populated and the subsequent DELETE of site settings unexecuted — a partially migrated, inconsistent state.

[ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? silently drops the 'embeddable hosts configured' condition that was part of the original contract — it now returns true whenever embed_truncate is on and the topic has an embed, even when no EmbeddableHost rows exist. A site that only uses feed polling (no inbound embeddable hosts) with embed_truncate enabled now shows the expand/truncate behavior on imported topics where the previous code deliberately gated it on hosts being configured; this behavior change to a public model method shipped inside a PR whose stated intent is only UI editing of host/category pairs.

[ADVISORY] The distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error was collapsed into 'invalid referer host', changing the observable error semantics for the not-configured case. Admins debugging a fresh install with zero EmbeddableHost rows now get 'invalid referer host' for every embed request, which points them at referer matching rather than at the real problem (no hosts configured yet); the distinguishing error string was part of the prior contract.

[ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost belongs_to :category but there is no dependent handling, so deleting a category (a normal admin action) leaves embeddable_hosts rows pointing at a nonexistent category_id while the column is null: false. After a category is deleted, the host row references a missing category; the admin UI's category-badge render and TopicEmbed.import's category assignment for that host degrade/break, and the host is effectively unusable until an admin re-edits it — the editing UI this PR introduces is also the only recovery path.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricator file was gutted to hold the embeddable_host fabricator while the full category fabricators were re-created in a new file, indicating a botched file move that leaves a misleading filename. The next developer looking for the category fabricator or adding to category_fabricator.rb will edit a file that actually defines embeddable_host; the mismatch between filename and content invites duplicate/conflicting fabricator definitions on the next change.

[ADVISORY] The global embed_category setting is replaced by per-host category with a silent fallback: when the feed URL's host has no matching EmbeddableHost record at import time, category becomes nil and PostCreator assigns the uncategorized category. Feed-polled topics from a host whose record was deleted (or whose saved host string failed the before_validation normalization, e.g. uppercase hosts rejected by the regex) silently land in Uncategorized instead of the intended category — a content-placement change that site owners will only notice by finding misplaced topics.

[BUG] The migration interpolates the former embeddable_hosts site-setting value directly into a SQL INSERT statement via string interpolation. A row value containing a single quote (any admin-saved host entry with an apostrophe or crafted quote) breaks out of the string literal, producing malformed/arbitrary SQL during the migration and an aborted/failed deploy; string-interpolated SQL is the injection class even when the source is a config store.

[BUG] The update action calls save_host on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, and destroy calls host.destroy on the same unguarded lookup. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a nonexistent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError (nil.host = / nil.destroy), returning a 500 instead of the 404 the admin API contract implies; a double-delete from the UI (stale row after concurrent edit) triggers it for staff users.

[ADVISORY] category_id is assigned from params without validating that the category exists or that the admin may post into it, and an invalid/foreign id is only caught (if at all) by the database FK. A staff user saving a host with a bogus category_id either fails with a raw DB constraint error (500) or, if no FK exists, creates an embeddable host pointing at a nonexistent category, so imported embed topics get a nil/invalid category; staff-only surface keeps impact moderate.

[BUG] The only test in this spec asserts the controller's superclass and nothing about its behavior, so create/update/destroy and the save_host logic (including the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id) can regress to total garbage while the suite stays green. Any breakage in create/update/destroy — e.g. a params[:embeddable_host] nil crash, a validation error rendering bug, or the category fallback disappearing — ships undetected; admins saving hosts get a 500 with no test signal.

[BUG] The only test asserts the controller's subclass relationship, so the show and update actions (update notably performs no persistence at all, and fetch_embedding's OpenStruct is never exercised end-to-end) have zero behavioral coverage. The embedding#update endpoint can silently stop returning hosts, return a 500 on an empty table, or (as currently written) never save anything, and this spec passes identically — the test provides false confidence that the admin embedding page is verified.

[ADVISORY] The fabricator files have swapped names: the file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) (and diff_category/happy_category/private_category), while spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host). Fabricators load regardless of filename so tests pass today, but the next developer adding a category fabricator edits category_fabricator.rb and collides with the embeddable_host definition there, or deletes what looks like a stray host fabricator in the category file; this is a git-rename accident being codified.

[ADVISORY] The topic_embed spec adds an embeddable_host fabricator only for the happy path, so the new branch in TopicEmbed.import where EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) returns false and category is passed as nil (eh.try(:category_id)) is never exercised by any test in the diff. A URL that fails host matching now creates a topic with category nil — PostCreator with an explicit nil category may reject or create uncategorized topics depending on validation — and whichever it is, no test pins it down, so a change to that behavior breaks silently.

[ADVISORY] The host_allowed? tests only cover hosts the record_for_host implementation already handles (valid URI with resolvable host), never the false-return paths the new code adds: an unparseable URI, a URI with no host, or a case mismatch between the stored host and uri.host — record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) without lowercasing the comparison argument, so 'http://Eviltrout.com' is rejected. The mirror tests pass while the case-sensitivity defect in record_for_host embeds content from legitimate mixed-case referers incorrectly rejected (or accepted, if a case-insensitive fix lands wrong) — the spec never distinguishes the intended semantics, so the next change to that query has no oracle.

[ADVISORY] The data migration that converts the old embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings into embeddable_hosts rows — including the raw SQL join, the uncategorized fallback, and the site_settings deletion — has no spec anywhere in the diff (checked spec/**: only embeddable_host_spec, topic_embed_spec, embed_controller_spec, topic_spec, site_setting_spec are touched, none references the migration). The fallback path `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no embed_category setting row exists (the query returns zero rows and [0] is nil), destroying every forum's embed configuration during upgrade, and nothing in the test suite would catch it before release.

[BUG] The backfill's cmd_tuples guard is dead for SELECTs in PostgreSQL, so the embeddable_hosts rows are never inserted while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old site settings. On a PostgreSQL production site with embeddable_hosts configured, execute('SELECT ...') returns a result whose cmd_tuples is always 0, the `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` branch never runs, and the subsequent `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` erases the admin's entire configured host list and embed category with zero rows migrated — all existing embeds return 'invalid referer host' and the data cannot be recovered without a backup.

[BUG] The backfill inserts old setting values verbatim into embeddable_hosts without the protocol/path trimming that both the old allows_embeddable_host? and the new EmbeddableHost model apply, so migrated rows fail the new exact-match lookup. A site whose setting was 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both explicitly supported by the old code and the updated controller specs) gets a row with host='http://discourse.org'; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then runs lower(host) = 'discourse.org' which never matches, so all embedding for that site breaks silently after the deploy even though the admin sees the host listed in the new UI.

[BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] on a SELECT that returns zero rows when the embed_category site setting has never been saved, crashing the migration. On any site where an admin never touched embedding settings, the INNER JOIN SELECT returns an empty result set, [0] is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError on nil['id'], halting db:migrate mid-deploy for every existing forum that never configured embedding — the common case, since the setting's default is ''.

[ADVISORY] The migration uses force: true on create_table and embeds raw model-free SQL, making a re-run destructive and the migration irreversible by design. If db:migrate is re-run against a schema where embeddable_hosts already exists (restore from backup, multi-statement run, or restore-and-replay), force: true silently drops the table and every host/category mapping admins have created since, with no rollback path because def change + data INSERT/DELETE leaves no down for the site_settings values it deletes.

[ADVISORY] Host values from the old setting are interpolated unescaped into the INSERT, so any value containing a quote or backslash breaks or corrupts the backfill. An admin whose embeddable_hosts setting contained a stray quote or odd hostname (the old free-text setting accepted anything) makes the generated INSERT a SQL syntax error or malformed row, aborting db:migrate after the table create but before site_settings cleanup — leaving the site in a half-migrated state with old settings still present and code already reading only the new table.

[BUG] update and destroy call methods on a possibly-nil record (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`), so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 where the admin API contract expects a 4xx/404. An admin editing two browser tabs who deletes a host in one and saves it in the other gets a raw 500 (nil.host= / nil.destroy), and the client's catch shows a generic popup instead of a meaningful 'not found'.

[BUG] The update action does not save anything — it re-renders the (unmodified) embedding as success, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a silent no-op reporting success. Admin saves embedding-level settings and receives a success response with unchanged data; any future settings fields added to this screen will be silently dropped while the UI believes they persisted.

[BUG] saveChanges calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` without returning the promise or attaching a rejection handler, so the caller resolves success before the request completes and a failure surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection with no user feedback. The admin clicking save gets no confirmation or error; on network failure the save silently never happens and nothing is shown in the UI.

[BUG] The delete action calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE (server error or network) is an unhandled rejection and the row is never removed but no error is shown to the admin. Admin clicks delete, confirms, sees the row still present with no explanation; the failure is invisible — contrast with save() which correctly uses popupAjaxError.

[BUG] After a successful save, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` is called with whatever the category-chooser holds; the server coerces a blank category_id to the uncategorized category while the client looks up the raw (blank/null) id, desynchronizing displayed state from persisted state. Admin who clears the category sees a blank/undefined category badge in the table while the server actually stored uncategorized_category_id — the UI misrepresents what was saved until reload.

[BUG] save_host dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` with no envelope guard, so a malformed request body (missing :embeddable_host key) raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 where the route contract expects a 4xx. Any client sending a create/update without the embeddable_host envelope (e.g. an out-of-date admin bundle after a rolling deploy) gets a raw 500 instead of a 400/422 error.

[ADVISORY] The embedding record is a hardcoded OpenStruct with id 'default' and update renders the same serialized payload including only embeddable_host IDs with no side-loaded host records, so any client that relies on the PUT response to refresh the hosts list will hydrate against stale/absent data. Future changes that re-render from the update response (as saveChanges implies) will show hosts as unresolved/blank records; the current code is a success-shaped no-op waiting to bite the next developer.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no index on host (and none on category_id), while every embed/comments request queries where("lower(host) = ?"). Each embed request is an unindexed, non-sargable (lower(host)) full scan; duplicates of the same host are freely insertable since there is no unique constraint, so admins create conflicting category mappings that resolve to whichever row .first returns. Operators get nondeterministic category assignment on duplicate rows.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `host` and `category_id` but adds no indexes and no uniqueness constraint. Runtime lookups use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` and is called on embed requests via `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (in `embed_controller.rb` and `topic_retriever.rb`). With no index, this forces a full table scan; and with no unique constraint, duplicate host rows are allowed, making `.first` pick an arbitrary row (DB-dependent), leading to nondeterministic category mapping in `TopicEmbed.import` (`eh.try(:category_id)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint and its client saveChanges() action are no-ops: update accepts no parameters, mutates nothing, and re-serializes the OpenStruct. The admin UI's save button (saveChanges in admin-embedding.js.es6) appears to succeed while persisting nothing, and the advertised update route is dead weight — a future maintainer adding a field to EmbeddingSerializer will find updates silently discarded because no assignment code exists anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows PUT /admin/customize/embedding is implemented but is a no-op: Admin::EmbeddingController#update just re-serializes @embedding (an OpenStruct built in fetch_embedding) and does not read params or persist anything. On the client, admin-embedding.js.es6 defines saveChanges() calling this.get('embedding').update({}), which would hit that PUT and similarly persist nothing. However, the provided admin template (embedding.hbs) does not include any “save changes” button/action hookup, and the only persistence shown is via embeddable-host component calling host.save/destroyRecord against Admin::EmbeddableHostsController. So the core concern (dead-weight/no-op endpoint that could mislead future changes) is valid, but the claim about an existing UI save button is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update and destroy fetch with .first and dereference the result without a nil check. A stale admin tab or raced delete sends an id that no longer exists and gets a NoMethodError 500 (nil.host= / nil.destroy) instead of a 404; there is no find_record-style guard so the error contract for this endpoint is an unhandled exception.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, both `update` and `destroy` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately dereference it (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If the record doesn’t exist (stale UI / raced delete / bad id), `host` is `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a handled 404 or error JSON.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? drops the 'any embeddable host configured' guard, so it now returns true for any topic with a topic_embed whenever embed_truncate is on, with no live host requirement. Sites that truncate embeds but have since deleted all allowed hosts still serve truncated/expandable first posts for historical embedded topics; the check's semantics changed from 'embedding actively configured' to 'embedding was ever used', and no caller was updated for that narrowing of the guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior guard in `Topic#expandable_first_post?`: it changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). Since `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting is also removed in this PR (config/site_settings.yml, app/models/site_setting.rb), there is no longer any check that embedding is currently configured (e.g., `EmbeddableHost.exists?`). This is a real, diff-grounded semantics change worth calling out, but the diff doesn’t prove it’s incorrect/broken—it's plausible the intended behavior is to allow expandability for historical embedded topics independent of current allowlist state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration permanently deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings with no down-migration and no archival, so the original configuration is irrecoverably destroyed the moment the migration runs. If the migration's data-copy logic misfires (e.g. the SQL-injection-prone string interpolation at line 28 hits a host value containing a quote and aborts mid-copy), the settings are already deleted and the operator's embed host list is lost; there is no rollback path since `change` provides only table-drop on rollback, not settings restoration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` explicitly deletes the old `site_settings` rows at the end (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`), and it does not provide any down-migration to restore them. That makes the old configuration unavailable for a downgrade/rollback scenario and is a legitimate migration-safety concern. However, the finding’s claim that a mid-copy failure would still leave settings deleted is not directly verifiable from the diff (migrations are often transactional, and the delete occurs after the inserts), and it also misstates rollback behavior (the presence of multiple `execute` calls makes this `change` migration effectively irreversible rather than “table-drop only”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Host values read from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into a raw SQL INSERT string ("... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."), so any value containing a single quote or backslash breaks the insert. A site whose embeddable_hosts setting contains an entry with an apostrophe raises a PG error mid-migration, leaving the table half-populated and the subsequent DELETE of site settings unexecuted — a partially migrated, inconsistent state.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, host values from the old `site_settings` row are split and interpolated directly into a raw SQL string: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-special characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid (or worse), causing the migration to error. This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness defect in the migration logic (it should use proper quoting/bind params). The finding’s point about leaving the DB in a partially migrated state is plausible depending on transactional DDL behavior, but regardless the unescaped interpolation itself is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] expandable_first_post? silently drops the 'embeddable hosts configured' condition that was part of the original contract — it now returns true whenever embed_truncate is on and the topic has an embed, even when no EmbeddableHost rows exist. A site that only uses feed polling (no inbound embeddable hosts) with embed_truncate enabled now shows the expand/truncate behavior on imported topics where the previous code deliberately gated it on hosts being configured; this behavior change to a public model method shipped inside a PR whose stated intent is only UI editing of host/category pairs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb), removing the “embeddable hosts configured” gate entirely. Since the old `embeddable_hosts` SiteSetting is removed and replaced by the `EmbeddableHost` table, the equivalent guard would now need to check something like `EmbeddableHost.exists?`, but no such check was added. This means the method can now return true even when there are zero `EmbeddableHost` rows, as long as `embed_truncate` is enabled and `has_topic_embed?` is true (and `TopicEmbed.import` does not require an EmbeddableHost record to create an embed; it only uses it for `category`, via `eh.try(:category_id)` in app/models/topic_embed.rb).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The distinct 'embeddable hosts not set' error was collapsed into 'invalid referer host', changing the observable error semantics for the not-configured case. Admins debugging a fresh install with zero EmbeddableHost rows now get 'invalid referer host' for every embed request, which points them at referer matching rather than at the real problem (no hosts configured yet); the distinguishing error string was part of the prior contract.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` removed the explicit `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` guard that raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set')` and now always raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('invalid referer host')` when `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` is false (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). With zero `EmbeddableHost` rows, `host_allowed?` returns false, so the not-configured case is no longer distinguishable by error string. This is an observable semantics/diagnostics change, but not a functional correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost belongs_to :category but there is no dependent handling, so deleting a category (a normal admin action) leaves embeddable_hosts rows pointing at a nonexistent category_id while the column is null: false. After a category is deleted, the host row references a missing category; the admin UI's category-badge render and TopicEmbed.import's category assignment for that host degrade/break, and the host is effectively unusable until an admin re-edits it — the editing UI this PR introduces is also the only recovery path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces EmbeddableHost with `belongs_to :category` and a `category_id` column declared `null: false` in the migration, but adds no foreign key constraint or lifecycle handling for category deletion (no `dependent:` behavior shown anywhere in the diff). If a Category is deleted, existing `embeddable_hosts` rows will keep a now-invalid `category_id`. The client component renders `{{category-badge host.category}}` and relies on the store hydrating `host.category` from `category_id`; with a missing category record this can become `null/undefined`. On the server, `TopicEmbed.import` passes `eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator` as the category, which can break if the id no longer exists. This is a real data integrity/correctness issue introduced by the new association/table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The category fabricator file was gutted to hold the embeddable_host fabricator while the full category fabricators were re-created in a new file, indicating a botched file move that leaves a misleading filename. The next developer looking for the category fabricator or adding to category_fabricator.rb will edit a file that actually defines embeddable_host; the mismatch between filename and content invites duplicate/conflicting fabricator definitions on the next change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced with a `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` definition, while the actual `Fabricator(:category)` and related category fabricators were moved into a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This creates a misleading filename/content mismatch (category_fabricator.rb no longer defines category), which is a maintainability/clarity problem and could confuse future changes or lead to accidental duplicate/conflicting fabricators later. It is not a directly verifiable runtime defect from this diff alone, but it is a concrete review issue grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The global embed_category setting is replaced by per-host category with a silent fallback: when the feed URL's host has no matching EmbeddableHost record at import time, category becomes nil and PostCreator assigns the uncategorized category. Feed-polled topics from a host whose record was deleted (or whose saved host string failed the before_validation normalization, e.g. uppercase hosts rejected by the regex) silently land in Uncategorized instead of the intended category — a content-placement change that site owners will only notice by finding misplaced topics.

adjudication.rationale: While the diff does remove the global `embed_category` setting and changes `TopicEmbed.import` to use a per-host category (`eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` then `category: eh.try(:category_id)`), the finding’s core claim that missing/deleted host records will silently create topics in Uncategorized is not shown or ensured by this diff. In fact, the authorization/allowlist checks were changed to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` and `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`), which would typically prevent imports when no matching `EmbeddableHost` exists. Also, the finding’s example about “uppercase hosts rejected by the regex” is contradicted by the model validation using a case-insensitive regex (`/.../i`), so uppercase hosts are not rejected by that validation per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration interpolates the former embeddable_hosts site-setting value directly into a SQL INSERT statement via string interpolation. A row value containing a single quote (any admin-saved host entry with an apostrophe or crafted quote) breaks out of the string literal, producing malformed/arbitrary SQL during the migration and an aborted/failed deploy; string-interpolated SQL is the injection class even when the source is a config store.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds an INSERT statement with direct string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes from the prior `site_settings` row (`embeddable_hosts`), and if it contains a single quote it will break the SQL string literal (and could allow SQL injection / at minimum cause migration failure). No escaping or parameterization is used in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update action calls save_host on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without a nil check, and destroy calls host.destroy on the same unguarded lookup. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a nonexistent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError (nil.host = / nil.destroy), returning a 500 instead of the 404 the admin API contract implies; a double-delete from the UI (stale row after concurrent edit) triggers it for staff users.
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that update/destroy retrieve EmbeddableHost via `where(...).first` without checking for nil, leading to NoMethodError when calling `save_host`/`destroy` on a nonexistent record—same issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] category_id is assigned from params without validating that the category exists or that the admin may post into it, and an invalid/foreign id is only caught (if at all) by the database FK. A staff user saving a host with a bogus category_id either fails with a raw DB constraint error (500) or, if no FK exists, creates an embeddable host pointing at a nonexistent category, so imported embed topics get a nil/invalid category; staff-only surface keeps impact moderate.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, `host.category_id` is set directly from `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` and then saved, with only a blank-check fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`—there is no validation that the category exists or is permitted (`belongs_to :category` has no presence/foreign-key validation shown, and the migration defines `category_id` as `null: false` but no FK constraint). This allows persisting an `embeddable_hosts` row pointing at a nonexistent category id, which then propagates to `TopicEmbed.import` where `category: eh.try(:category_id)` is passed, potentially causing incorrect/nil category behavior or runtime errors depending on downstream handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only test in this spec asserts the controller's superclass and nothing about its behavior, so create/update/destroy and the save_host logic (including the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id) can regress to total garbage while the suite stays green. Any breakage in create/update/destroy — e.g. a params[:embeddable_host] nil crash, a validation error rendering bug, or the category fallback disappearing — ships undetected; admins saving hosts get a 500 with no test signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` with nontrivial behavior in `create/update/destroy` and `save_host` (e.g., `params[:embeddable_host]` access, validation error handling, and fallback `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`). However, the only added spec for this controller (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb`) merely asserts it subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any of that behavior, so regressions in these actions/logic would not be caught. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a direct functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only test asserts the controller's subclass relationship, so the show and update actions (update notably performs no persistence at all, and fetch_embedding's OpenStruct is never exercised end-to-end) have zero behavioral coverage. The embedding#update endpoint can silently stop returning hosts, return a 500 on an empty table, or (as currently written) never save anything, and this spec passes identically — the test provides false confidence that the admin embedding page is verified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new controllers Admin::EmbeddingController and Admin::EmbeddableHostsController, but the only new controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb and embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb) merely assert subclassing and do not exercise any behavior of `show`, `update`, or `fetch_embedding`. In particular, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is implemented as just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` with no persistence, yet the admin UI calls `embedding.update({})` (admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6). The finding about “false confidence” from these trivial specs is grounded, though the specific failure modes mentioned are speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fabricator files have swapped names: the file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines Fabricator(:category) (and diff_category/happy_category/private_category), while spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host). Fabricators load regardless of filename so tests pass today, but the next developer adding a category fabricator edits category_fabricator.rb and collides with the embeddable_host definition there, or deletes what looks like a stray host fabricator in the category file; this is a git-rename accident being codified.
matched_golden_ids: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that the contents/definitions in `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` and `category_fabricator.rb` are swapped (category fabricators in the host file and vice versa), noting this likely came from a rename accident and can cause future errors/collisions. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about swapped contents and loss/misplacement of the original category fabricators.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The topic_embed spec adds an embeddable_host fabricator only for the happy path, so the new branch in TopicEmbed.import where EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) returns false and category is passed as nil (eh.try(:category_id)) is never exercised by any test in the diff. A URL that fails host matching now creates a topic with category nil — PostCreator with an explicit nil category may reject or create uncategorized topics depending on validation — and whichever it is, no test pins it down, so a change to that behavior breaks silently.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff introduces `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to `PostCreator` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `record_for_host` returns nil/false (e.g., well-formed URL but no matching `EmbeddableHost`), `category` becomes nil. The updated `topic_embed_spec` adds `let!(:embeddable_host) { Fabricate(:embeddable_host) }` and asserts the happy path category mapping, but there is no test covering the new nil-category branch (no matching host) to pin down intended behavior. Whether that nil is acceptable/blocked is not shown in the diff, so this is best classified as a specific missing-test/edge-case concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The host_allowed? tests only cover hosts the record_for_host implementation already handles (valid URI with resolvable host), never the false-return paths the new code adds: an unparseable URI, a URI with no host, or a case mismatch between the stored host and uri.host — record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host) without lowercasing the comparison argument, so 'http://Eviltrout.com' is rejected. The mirror tests pass while the case-sensitivity defect in record_for_host embeds content from legitimate mixed-case referers incorrectly rejected (or accepted, if a case-insensitive fix lands wrong) — the spec never distinguishes the intended semantics, so the next change to that query has no oracle.
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that record_for_host uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without lowercasing the parameter, causing mixed-case `uri.host` values (e.g., `Eviltrout.com`) not to match intended case-insensitive comparison. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The data migration that converts the old embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings into embeddable_hosts rows — including the raw SQL join, the uncategorized fallback, and the site_settings deletion — has no spec anywhere in the diff (checked spec/**: only embeddable_host_spec, topic_embed_spec, embed_controller_spec, topic_spec, site_setting_spec are touched, none references the migration). The fallback path `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no embed_category setting row exists (the query returns zero rows and [0] is nil), destroying every forum's embed configuration during upgrade, and nothing in the test suite would catch it before release.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` does `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If that query returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, so `['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration/upgrade (and thus potentially losing or blocking migration of embed configuration). The diff includes no tests covering this migration path, so the failure would not be caught by the touched specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backfill's cmd_tuples guard is dead for SELECTs in PostgreSQL, so the embeddable_hosts rows are never inserted while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old site settings. On a PostgreSQL production site with embeddable_hosts configured, execute('SELECT ...') returns a result whose cmd_tuples is always 0, the `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` branch never runs, and the subsequent `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` erases the admin's entire configured host list and embed category with zero rows migrated — all existing embeds return 'invalid referer host' and the data cannot be recovered without a backup.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration loads the old setting via `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and then gates the backfill on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. For PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` on a SELECT result is typically 0 (rows returned are accessed via `ntuples` / array access), so this condition can prevent any insert backfill even when the SELECT returned a row. The migration then unconditionally runs `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would erase the prior configuration without migrating it, matching the described data-loss scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backfill inserts old setting values verbatim into embeddable_hosts without the protocol/path trimming that both the old allows_embeddable_host? and the new EmbeddableHost model apply, so migrated rows fail the new exact-match lookup. A site whose setting was 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' (both explicitly supported by the old code and the updated controller specs) gets a row with host='http://discourse.org'; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then runs lower(host) = 'discourse.org' which never matches, so all embedding for that site breaks silently after the deploy even though the admin sees the host listed in the new UI.
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe that the migration/backfill inserts embeddable_hosts via raw SQL using unnormalized values (including protocol and/or path), bypassing the model’s normalization. As a result, the new lookup that compares only the bare host fails to match migrated rows, breaking existing embedding configurations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] on a SELECT that returns zero rows when the embed_category site setting has never been saved, crashing the migration. On any site where an admin never touched embedding settings, the INNER JOIN SELECT returns an empty result set, [0] is nil, and the migration raises NoMethodError on nil['id'], halting db:migrate mid-deploy for every existing forum that never configured embedding — the common case, since the setting's default is ''.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` on an INNER JOIN selecting the embed_category setting. If that SELECT returns 0 rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row for `embed_category`), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, preventing the later `if category_id == 0` fallback from running. This crash is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration uses force: true on create_table and embeds raw model-free SQL, making a re-run destructive and the migration irreversible by design. If db:migrate is re-run against a schema where embeddable_hosts already exists (restore from backup, multi-statement run, or restore-and-replay), force: true silently drops the table and every host/category mapping admins have created since, with no rollback path because def change + data INSERT/DELETE leaves no down for the site_settings values it deletes.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, causing silent data loss of any previously configured embeddable hosts. The same migration uses `def change` with raw `execute` INSERTs and then `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, making the migration effectively irreversible (no `down` to restore deleted settings/data). Both concerns are directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Host values from the old setting are interpolated unescaped into the INSERT, so any value containing a quote or backslash breaks or corrupts the backfill. An admin whose embeddable_hosts setting contained a stray quote or odd hostname (the old free-text setting accepted anything) makes the generated INSERT a SQL syntax error or malformed row, aborting db:migrate after the table create but before site_settings cleanup — leaving the site in a half-migrated state with old settings still present and code already reading only the new table.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` backfills rows via raw SQL string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The value `h` comes directly from the previous `site_settings` value (`val.split("\n")`) and is not escaped/quoted safely. Any host containing a single quote or other special characters would produce invalid SQL and abort the migration after `create_table` but before `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings ..."`, leaving the DB in a partially migrated state. This defect is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy call methods on a possibly-nil record (`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`), so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 where the admin API contract expects a 4xx/404. An admin editing two browser tabs who deletes a host in one and saves it in the other gets a raw 500 (nil.host= / nil.destroy), and the client's catch shows a generic popup instead of a meaningful 'not found'.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then used without a nil-check (`save_host(host)` and `host.destroy`). If the id is missing/already deleted, `host` will be `nil` and calling `host.host=` or `host.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a 404/4xx.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update action does not save anything — it re-renders the (unmodified) embedding as success, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a silent no-op reporting success. Admin saves embedding-level settings and receives a success response with unchanged data; any future settings fields added to this screen will be silently dropped while the UI believes they persisted.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, the method indeed does not apply any params and simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`) via `render_serialized`, so a PUT would be a no-op. However, the diff’s UI (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) does not expose any embedding-level settings nor a save button that triggers `saveChanges`; it only manages `EmbeddableHost` records via the separate `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (create/update/destroy). So while the update endpoint/action looks incomplete/misleading (and could silently drop future fields), the claim about admins “saving embedding-level settings and receiving success with unchanged data” isn’t currently verifiable from this diff because there are no such settings to save on this screen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] saveChanges calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` without returning the promise or attaching a rejection handler, so the caller resolves success before the request completes and a failure surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection with no user feedback. The admin clicking save gets no confirmation or error; on network failure the save silently never happens and nothing is shown in the UI.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` and does not return the resulting value or attach a `.catch(...)`/error handler. That is a concrete, diff-grounded issue because any rejection from `update` (if it returns a promise as is typical for model updates in this codebase) would not be handled here. However, the finding’s claims about “admin clicking save” and “no confirmation/error in the UI” aren’t directly verifiable from the diff because the new `embedding.hbs` template does not include any save button or wiring to `saveChanges`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE (server error or network) is an unhandled rejection and the row is never removed but no error is shown to the admin. Admin clicks delete, confirms, sees the row still present with no explanation; the failure is invisible — contrast with save() which correctly uses popupAjaxError.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` without any `.catch(...)` error handling, unlike `save()` which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the DELETE request fails (server/network), the rejection is unhandled and no admin-visible error is shown; the row will remain because `deleteHost` is only sent on success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] After a successful save, `Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId'))` is called with whatever the category-chooser holds; the server coerces a blank category_id to the uncategorized category while the client looks up the raw (blank/null) id, desynchronizing displayed state from persisted state. Admin who clears the category sees a blank/undefined category badge in the table while the server actually stored uncategorized_category_id — the UI misrepresents what was saved until reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and, after `host.save(props)` succeeds, forcibly sets the relationship with `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));`. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly coerces a blank category to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (`host.category_id = ... if host.category_id.blank?`). If the chooser yields `null`/blank, the server persists uncategorized but the client still looks up `findById(null)` and sets `category` to `undefined`, so the UI can display a blank badge despite saving uncategorized. The diff does not show any client-side use of the returned `category_id` to correct this, so the desync is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] save_host dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` with no envelope guard, so a malformed request body (missing :embeddable_host key) raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 where the route contract expects a 4xx. Any client sending a create/update without the embeddable_host envelope (e.g. an out-of-date admin bundle after a rolling deploy) gets a raw 500 instead of a 400/422 error.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, lines in `save_host`). If the request body omits the `:embeddable_host` key, `params[:embeddable_host]` is nil and this will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a controlled 4xx response. The diff shows no guard (`require`, presence check, or safe navigation) to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embedding record is a hardcoded OpenStruct with id 'default' and update renders the same serialized payload including only embeddable_host IDs with no side-loaded host records, so any client that relies on the PUT response to refresh the hosts list will hydrate against stale/absent data. Future changes that re-render from the update response (as saveChanges implies) will show hosts as unresolved/blank records; the current code is a success-shaped no-op waiting to bite the next developer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` builds a hardcoded `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `#update` does not apply any params/persistence—it just re-renders the same serialized embedding (a “success-shaped” no-op). However, the finding’s claim that the response contains *only* `embeddable_host` IDs with *no* side-loaded host records is not verifiable from the diff and is likely a misread: `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which typically implies IDs plus side-loaded records in Discourse’s REST serializer flow. The real, diff-grounded issue is the misleading no-op update endpoint/client action, not proven missing sideloading.
